item.title: Thanksgiving at Songbird Parlour — Wed Nov 25 — 14301 Arnold Dr #3
item.description:
Thanksgiving at Songbird Parlour in Glen Ellen offers a festive holiday dining experience in a historic 1839 Victorian setting. Guests can celebrate with two special dining opportunities. Thanksgiving Eve, Wednesday, November 25, 2026, from 5–9 p.m., features the restaurant’s popular Prime Rib Night, with slow-roasted prime rib, seasonal sides, horseradish, au jus, and chives. The regular menu will also be available. On Thanksgiving Day, Thursday, November 26, 2026, from 1–4 p.m., guests can enjoy an à la carte menu along with seasonal chef specials, making it easy to celebrate without spending the holiday in the kitchen. Reservations are recommended, as holiday tables are expected to fill quickly.

item.title: Santa Rosa Turkey Trot at Old Courthouse Square — Thu Nov 26, 6:30 AM — Santa Rosa
item.description:
The Santa Rosa Turkey Trot brings the community together on Thanksgiving morning for a festive run through downtown Santa Rosa. Starting at Old Courthouse Square, participants can enjoy a 5K race or the Tiny Turkey dash for children under five. The route winds through downtown and along the Santa Rosa Creek, offering a fun way for runners, walkers, and families to celebrate the holiday. Costumes are welcome, and participants can look forward to finisher medals and awards. The annual event also supports the Redwood Empire Food Bank, helping fight food insecurity throughout Sonoma County. The race takes place rain or shine.
Source: Sonoma.com, North Bay Bohemian, Visit Santa Rosa

item.title: Family Hike at Sugarloaf — Fri Nov 27, 10:00 AM — Sugarloaf Ridge State Park
item.description:
Join our Docents on this fun family hike that is good for all ages, where you will learn about Sugarloaf Park, its plants, animals, and history.
The hike begins from the Visitor Center. One option heads down to the waterfall on the 2-mile Pony Gate-Canyon loop, while a second, shorter option will meander along the Creekside Nature Trail. Please note the route is bound to change depending on logistics such as wet crossings and the participants' physical ability. Free event, RSVP required. Wear layers, appropriate footwear for slippery/rocky trails, bring at least 32oz of water, sun protection, and if desired, a snack. Parking fees apply.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat, Visit Santa Rosa

item.description:
New Moon Circus Presents ‘La Lune Brille’: a highly original, all-human circus that enchants through breathtaking acrobatics and athletically stunning skill.
Sonoma, CA— November 27 - Dec 27 – This 2026 winter season, New Moon Circus invites audiences to ‘La Lune Brille’ — memorable family fun and stunning artistry under the intimate and charming atmosphere of the ‘petite’ big top.
Meet the Winter moon and her frenemy, the Sun. When the moon is pushed from the sky, she must find a way home to the stars. Come along the journey as she encounters mysterious beings and friendly creatures on the way.
A child pleasing origin myth told through impressive aerialists, jugglers, acrobats, and clever comedy, this show blends classic storybook atmosphere with celestial magic. La Lune Brille will surprise, dazzle and delight all ages.

item.title: Willy Tea Taylor & Cassandra Lewis — Sat Nov 28, 7:00 PM — HopMonk Tavern Novato
item.description:
Willy Tea Taylor is a father, brother, and son. His remarkable ability to sing about profound subjects in a simple way makes his songs a great place to lose yourself. Much of that comes from his upbringing.
Willy grew up surrounded by rolling hills and horses in the small town of Oakdale, California. Known as the “Cowboy Capital of the World” for breeding so many world champion rodeo cowboys, Oakdale is still Willy’s home and the setting for many of his songs.
Despite coming from a long line of cattlemen – his grandfather Walt was one of the most respected of his generation – Willy’s first love was baseball. As a catcher, he had a gift for the nuances of calling a game from behind the plate. When a knee injury ended his ability to catch, Willy turned his attention to music.

item.title: New Moon Circus Presents ‘La Lune Brille — Sun Nov 29, 1:00 PM — CORNERSTONE SONOMA - Under the Big Top Tent
item.description:
New Moon Circus Presents ‘La Lune Brille’: a highly original, all-human circus that enchants through breathtaking acrobatics and athletically stunning skill.
Sonoma, CA— November 27 - Dec 27 – This 2026 winter season, New Moon Circus invites audiences to ‘La Lune Brille’ — memorable family fun and stunning artistry under the intimate and charming atmosphere of the ‘petite’ big top.
Meet the Winter moon and her frenemy, the Sun. When the moon is pushed from the sky, she must find a way home to the stars. Come along the journey as she encounters mysterious beings and friendly creatures on the way.
A child pleasing origin myth told through impressive aerialists, jugglers, acrobats, and clever comedy, this show blends classic storybook atmosphere with celestial magic. La Lune Brille will surprise, dazzle and delight all ages.

item.title: Patron Saints of Influence Fall Reading + Open Mic — Sun Nov 29, 4:00 PM — Shady Oak Barrel House
item.description:
The next Patron Saints literary reading & open mic will pay homage to mother of science fiction Mary Shelley with featured readings by Lauren C. Johnson, Shawna Swetech, and Wendy M. Thompson.
As always, you are welcome to share your own written work in 5 minutes or less during the open mic. All words are welcome as long as they're not hateful or AI-generated.
About the featured readers:
Lauren C. Johnson attributes her upbringing in Florida–America’s weirdest state–to her interest in the ecological and surreal. She's the interviews editor for The Racket Journal, where she champions experimental literature, and is a co-founder and editor of Club Chicxulub, a speculative fiction journal and reading series that amplifies emerging authors. She also co-hosts Babylon Salon, one of the longest-running reading series in the Bay Area. item.title: "People of the West: Gold Rush" Screening, Presentation & Nature Walk — Wed Dec 2, 6:00 PM — SSU Stevenson Hall 1301 and Native Plant Garden
item.description:
Join us for our third “People of the West” screening, where we watch the "Gold Rush" episode, which covers California's mid-1800s transformation — marked by conquest, massacres, and betrayal. Following the presentation and discussion, participants will hear a half-hour presentation by Archaeologist Mark Selverston on research and cultural resource projects he's undertaken at prominent Gold Rush and state park locations. We'll then have the opportunity to take part in a gentle walk along the Copeland Creek Trail to the Native Plant Garden, where we can rest and reflect with nature. Dinner will be provided!
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat
